issues.title: Malformed boundary condition invalidates the discrete problem
issues.failure_explanation: The condition mid(γ′)=0 is a geometric assertion independent of the candidate function. It cannot define the intended homogeneous-boundary Crouzeix–Raviart space. Consequently the construction u_h=argmin_{v_h∈V_h} J(v_h) in eq:CRfem has either an empty admissible set or the wrong boundary contract. The corrected condition v_h(mid(γ′))=0 restores the boundary degrees of freedom used throughout the paper.
issues.overall_effect: The discrete solution and the interpolation/companion constructions using V_h are not well-defined with the stated homogeneous boundary condition, so the main and both localized a priori chains are affected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the definition of V_h, replace “mid(γ′) = 0” by “v_h(mid(γ′)) = 0” for every boundary face, and read every subsequent use of V_h with this homogeneous Crouzeix–Raviart boundary condition. No proof or theorem statement otherwise needs alteration.
issues.why_classification: The set comprehension, the homogeneous W_0^{1,1} problem, the CR interpolation, and the companion mapping into S_0^1 uniquely force the missing evaluation of v_h. This is a transcriptional omission of the candidate function, and inserting it requires no mathematical inference or construction.

issues.title: Main proof drops the convex conjugate
issues.failure_explanation: The face-residual estimate preceding the displayed conclusion contains (φ_{|∇_h v_h|})* applied to h|f|, and Young's inequality also pairs the companion error with that conjugate. The old summary instead writes φ_{|∇_h v_h|}(h|f|). For a general uniformly convex N-function the primal and conjugate have different growth, and lem:Oscillation controls only the conjugate quantity, so the final invocation does not close the proof.
issues.overall_effect: The old proof of the main quasi-optimality theorem retains an uncontrolled source term, and the nonconforming localized estimate that invokes the main theorem is consequently not established by that chain.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restore the omitted conjugation star in the concluding source term of Step 1, writing the integral of (φ_{|∇_h v_h|})* applied to h_T|f|, and retain that dual term when collecting the estimates in Step 4. Lemma Oscillation then closes the main proof, and the derivation of thm:Apriori is unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The preceding face-residual calculation, Young inequality, Step 2, and lem:Oscillation all already use the conjugate quantity. They uniquely force the starred expression, so this is a copied-symbol error rather than a missing argument or a change to any stated guarantee.

issues.title: Higher-order oscillation is claimed without qualifying assumptions

failure_location.quote: Theorem~\ref{thm:mainResult}, verified in Section~\ref{sec:MediusAnalysis}, marks the first a priori error estimate for non-conforming approximations for $p$-Laplace type problems that bounds the error by a best-approximation error plus a higher-order data oscillation term.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Given a uniformly convex N-function $\phi\colon [0,\infty) \to \mathbb{R}$ (see Definition~\ref{eq:defNfunction} below) and a right-hand side $f\in L^\infty(\Omega)$

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the estimate contains a higher-order data oscillation term in the general setting of a uniformly convex N-function and f∈L∞. The old formal material establishes the quasi-optimal estimate with osc, defines osc in eq:DefOsc, and compares shifted oscillations in lem:Oscillation, but gives no mesh-rate showing that osc is of higher order than the approximation error. The new remark obtains an explicit h-gain only after assuming differentiability and index bounds for φ and sufficient smoothness of f. Thus the unqualified rate characterization exceeds what the old paper supports.
issues.overall_effect: The formal quasi-optimality estimate remains a bound with data oscillation, but the introduction materially overstates the generally guaranteed asymptotic character of that term.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the unqualified description by the supported statement that the estimate contains a best-approximation error plus a data oscillation term, and remove the corresponding unqualified “higher-order” characterization wherever it is made under only uniform convexity and f∈L∞. The formal quasi-optimality estimate itself remains unchanged.
issues.why_classification: Removing “higher-order” withdraws a substantive asymptotic-rate characterization, so the correction is not a typo or a no-loss minor edit. The loss is nevertheless limited: the same error estimate and data-oscillation term remain, and only a local prose claim must be weakened, with no reconstruction of the formal results.

issues.title: Jensen is applied with a varying shift
issues.failure_explanation: The prose invokes Jensen to compare φ_{|∇u(x)|}(|Π_0(∇u-χ_T)|) with the average of φ_{|∇u(x)|}(|∇u-χ_T|). Jensen requires one fixed convex function on the averaging element, whereas the shift |∇u(x)| is spatially varying. By eq:Ince, ∇_h I_NC u=Π_0∇u is elementwise constant, so using that shift makes Jensen valid; a subsequent shift-change and absorption recover the claimed best-approximation bound.
issues.overall_effect: The interpolation estimate closing thm:Apriori is not established as written. Its later reuse in the conforming interpolation theorem and the conforming a priori estimate is likewise unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rewrite eq:approxInc using the elementwise constant shift |∇_h I_NC u|=|Π_0∇u|. Apply Jensen elementwise with this fixed shift, then use the already stated shift-change estimate to return to the comparison shift |∇u| and absorb the resulting interpolation-error term. Use this corrected estimate in thm:ApproxProperties and thm:AprioriConf.
issues.why_classification: The varying-shift Jensen step is a genuine invalid inference, so it is not a typo. Its repair is short, local, and routine using the commuting identity, Jensen, and the existing shift-change proposition; it preserves every affected statement, hypothesis, rate, and conclusion.

issues.title: Companion estimate omits boundary-face control

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\nodes(\Omega)$ denote the set of interior vertices in $\tria$.

issues.failure_explanation: Under the uniquely forced homogeneous Crouzeix–Raviart boundary condition, take a square split into two triangles and assign cyclic boundary-vertex values 1,-1,1,-1 to a globally conforming piecewise-affine function. Every boundary-edge midpoint value is zero and the interior tangential gradient jump is zero, but the conforming companion has zero boundary vertices and differs from the function. Thus the left-hand side of eq:Enrichment is positive while its old interior-face right-hand side is zero. The proof's interior-node averaging argument cannot be applied to boundary vertices.
issues.overall_effect: Both parts of the companion lemma lack boundary control, so every later proof using the companion estimate—including the main, nonconforming, interpolation, and conforming a priori results—has an unclosed boundary contribution.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define one-sided gradient and tangential jumps on boundary faces and replace the interior-face sum in eq:Enrichment and its ensuing raw companion bounds by a sum over all faces. Add the boundary-vertex estimate obtained from v_h(mid(γ))=0 and the boundary-face bubble argument using the zero trace of the conforming comparison function. Use the resulting boundary-corrected companion estimates throughout the four listed dependent results, whose final guarantees can remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The interior-face-only estimate is genuinely false and cannot be retained, as the stated counterexample shows. A complete repair therefore adds an essential boundary residual and a nontrivial boundary case to both parts of the companion argument. This is a contained, standard extension with only a limited weakening of the lemma and no loss of the downstream theorems, so it is moderate rather than serious.

issues.title: Wrong discrete jump in the companion shift change
issues.failure_explanation: Applying the stated shift-change estimate with shifts |∇v_h(T_j)| and |∇v_h(T_{j+1})| produces δ|F(∇v_h(T_j))-F(∇v_h(T_{j+1}))|², which is equivalent to a shifted jump term for ∇_h v_h. Equation eq:Proofaaassskkkkk- replaces this by a jump of ∇_h e_h. Since e_h=v_h-u_h and u_h is arbitrary, that replacement and the ensuing absorption into e_h-jump terms are unavailable. The later case split on A(∇_h e_h) therefore does not control the actual shift-change remainder.
issues.overall_effect: The general nonlinear companion estimate is not proved, and the old direct proof of the main quasi-optimality theorem and its nonconforming a priori consequence lose the companion control they invoke.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the shift-change remainder, replace the jump of ∇_h e_h by the forced jump of ∇_h v_h and do not absorb it into the e_h-jump sum. Reformulate the companion bound to retain a small multiple of the resulting v_h-jump functional, and prove a separate bound for that functional against a conforming comparison w and the dual residual (φ_{|∇_h v_h|})*(h_T|div A(∇w)|), using lem:TwoCases and the existing bubble arguments. Apply this bound with w=u in thm:mainResult and then invoke the repaired main theorem in thm:Apriori.
issues.why_classification: The wrong jump is used essentially in the old absorption and case split, so changing one symbol alone does not repair the proof. A complete resolution needs a contained but nontrivial auxiliary jump estimate and reorganization of the companion invocations. It retains the same medius architecture and the full main and a priori guarantees, avoiding both global reconstruction and major mathematical loss.

issues.title: Approximation theorem uses the wrong comparison variable

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For any $v\in W^{1,1}_0(\Omega)$ one has the interpolation error

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem quantifies every v∈W^{1,1}_0(Ω), and its left-hand side and interpolation construction depend on v. Nevertheless, its old right-hand side and the final proof invocation use F(∇u). The cited interpolation calculation, when applied to the theorem's input, yields the corresponding minimum for F(∇v). Thus the proof supports a different, v-dependent conclusion. The later use in thm:AprioriConf specializes v=u, so that later result is not additionally affected by this variable mismatch alone.
issues.overall_effect: The approximation theorem is not established for its advertised arbitrary input v; only the specialization v=u is consistent with the written comparison term.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace F(∇u) by F(∇v) in the comparison minimum in thm:ApproxProperties and in the corresponding final invocation in its proof. No downstream change is needed because thm:AprioriConf already specializes the approximation theorem to v=u.
issues.why_classification: The theorem quantifies v, its interpolation operator and left-hand side depend on v, and the cited calculation directly yields the v-dependent minimum. These features uniquely force the variable correction, which requires no new inference and does not alter the intended interpolation guarantee.

issues.title: Approximation theorem drops the convex conjugate
issues.failure_explanation: The second interpolation addend is bounded by lem:confComp, whose residual is (φ_{|∇v|})*(h|div A(∇v)|) after the appropriate shift comparison. Nothing in the old proof converts that dual quantity into φ_{|∇v|}(h|div A(∇v)|), and the two have different growth for a general uniformly convex N-function. Hence the invoked result supports the conjugate residual, not the theorem's stated primal residual.
issues.overall_effect: The general conforming interpolation estimate is stated with an unsupported residual quantity, and the conforming a priori proof cannot legitimately pass from that primal term to lem:Oscillation's conjugate oscillation control.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the primal residual by the conjugate residual ∫(φ_{|∇v|})*(h_T|div A(∇v)|) throughout thm:ApproxProperties, its proof, and related explanatory text. Carry the conjugate quantity through thm:AprioriConf and use the conjugate shift-change estimate followed by lem:Oscillation. The hypotheses, interpolation error, best-approximation term, and final conforming a priori estimate can otherwise remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: Although the proof uniquely supplies the conjugate, the formal theorem as written promises a coherent residual with generally different growth. Replacing it can change the residual rate and is therefore not a typo or a no-loss minor correction. The corrected estimate remains recognizably the same interpolation theorem and supports the full dependent chain through local changes, so the loss and repair burden are moderate rather than serious.
